## Abstract

We study mixed moments of logarithmic derivatives and characteristic polynomials of Haar unitary matri-ces at independent complex exponents. A planar Toeplitz determinant, radial Mellin readout, and physical branch connections relate finite-rank formulas to fixed-interior, microscopic, and circle limits. This complete cumulative edition retains the full 25-section foundation and integrates twelve subsequent constructions. At ranks three through eight, finite exact-arithmetic absolute approximations now cover the full radius interval 0 ≤z ≤ 0.9 on the original independent complex order and tilt box. Effective Bessel remainders, complete signed populations, balanced tails, and separately priced preparation, image, and arithmetic returns establish the joins. Actual finite-arithmetic certificates remain distinct from the common formulas and do not assert uniform relative accuracy or bounded runtime. A configurable physical-source arithmetic construction and targeted source/image refinements certify diffi-cult near-zero scalar readouts. For rank eight, correlated original-Haar majorants, coherent analytic terminal projection, and phase-aware parameter enclosures give one connected simple-zero branch for |h| ≤ 0.20 and 0.899 ≤z ≤ 0.9. In the moving predictor tube the uniqueness radius is 0.012, the zero lies within radius 0.01, and T = (s −α)G with |G| > 1/1300. The stronger inner theorem on |h| ≤ 0.18 has uniqueness radius 0.006, 8 zero radius 0.004537, and factor 1/625. Proofs, exact predictor data, numerical evidence, failed controls, and remaining obligations are presented with their individual domains. Earlier asymptotic and full-state results retain their original hypotheses and attribution. The quantitative continuation joins the complex scalar from the exact circle through positive microscopic depths to the interior Gaussian comparison at the actual radius. The small-depth error separates a power of depth from a negative power of log rank. At larger depths a radius-corrected approximation has uniform normalized error of order N^{−1} times a power of 1 + log N. Retaining the finite-rank one-angle term gives an additive rate through the upper moment threshold. A direct absolute-refinement theorem covers ordinary finite ranks, with an executed rank-two quadrature on independent complex inputs. The microscopic certification continuation gives computable Fourier-tail estimates for independent complex tilt on arbitrary compact positive-depth and tilt sets. It implements a complete Mellin budget and validates alternative coefficient enclosures, including nonreal and inverse-order controls. The general bound has large numerical constants, and the executions distinguish direct quadrature, near-integer reductions and large-depth comparisons. At depth one, an effective rank comparison and a shifted positive Gram estimate now give usable Fourier budgets at small cutoffs for an independent complex fractional order. A validated contour Hankel quadrature closes a nonzero scalar enclosure at that tuple. Explicit singular-value deficit estimates also price higher accuracy tails, at cutoffs exceeding the present retained-integral calculation. At c = 1, h = 1/2 + i/8, s = 1/2 + i/20, signed frequency windows and measured Bessel averages of the matched positive Haar law give an absolute disk of radius below 0.000263563 for the independent complex coefficient, with |F| > 0.51513048. The claim map following the contents traces the complete disk, the connected asymptotic theorem, finite-rank refinement, and the conditional zeta prediction to their mathematical and numerical inputs.

## Fixed-size mixed moments and their domains

## 1. Fixed-size mixed moments and their domains

Let U have normalized Haar measure on U(N), let λ_{j} denote its eigenvalues, and take z real with 0 ≤z < 1. Define

$$
\Lambda_N(z)=\det(I-zU),\qquad S_N(z)=\sum_{j=1}^{N}\frac{(1-z^2)\lambda_j}{1-z\lambda_j}=-(1-z^2)\frac{\Lambda_N'(z)}{\Lambda_N(z)}.
$$

For complex h, s define the expectation, in its domain of absolute integrability on U(N),

$$
T_N(h,s;z)=\mathbb E\bigl[|S_N(z)|^{2h}|\Lambda_N(z)|^{2s}\bigr].
$$

Positive bases use the real logarithm. Values on Haar-null zero sets can be assigned arbitrarily. The diagonal s = h recovers the derivative moment multiplied by (1 −z^{2})^{2h}.

Theorem 1.1 (fixed-size moment formulas).

Write D_{N}(ζ) for the determinant in (1.1), and Φ(ρ) for its circular average, also denoted  ̄φ(ρ). The radial Mellin formula (5.3), the Gaussian planar limit (5.2), and the derivative formula (5.4) hold on the following domains. Each finite lower entry a denotes the strict inequality Re h > a. The derivative column also requires Re h < 1 before applying Laplacians.

| Matrix size and location | Absolute moment | Mellin and Gaussian limits | Derivative limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N ≥ 3, 0 ≤ z < 1 | −1 | −1 | −1 |
| N = 2, 0 < z < 1 | −1 | −1 | −3/4 |
| N = 2, z = 0 | −1/2 | −1/2 | −1/2 |
| N = 1, 0 < z < 1 | all h | −1 | −1/2 |
| N = 1, z = 0 | all h | −3/4 | −1/4 |

At nonnegative integer h, the Mellin formula is evaluated by its removable limit, which gives the integer moment. For N = 2, 0 < z < 1, the Mellin tail alone exists even for −5/4 < Re h ≤−1. The table describes equality with the ordinary Haar expectation. Estimates are for fixed N. On compact parameter sets in the interior of each stated regime the proof yields locally uniform estimates. In a conditionally convergent region, integrating a planar kernel means truncating to disks centered at zero.

## Frequencies of the leading saddles

For even N there is a single balanced saddle class. Its directional frequency is Nz Re u. It vanishes in every direction at z = 0 and on the two imaginary rays for every real z > 0. For odd N the balanced frequencies are Nz Re u ± 1. Both undifferentiated coefficients are nonzero, and at least one frequency is nonzero, although one can vanish. At z = 0 with even N every positive-order source derivative has zero leading coefficient because S = 0. Thus the common derivative estimate is an upper bound. As normalization checks, (N, z) = (1, 0) N/2,N/2 gives J (ρ) and (N, z) = (2, 0) gives J (ρ)^{2} + J (ρ)^{2}∼ 2/(πρ). 0 0 1

The companion rank2_check.py derives the integer-moment polynomials from the exact Taylor coefficients of the Bessel determinant and rotational symmetry, then tests every coefficient of the differential equation in rational arithmetic for h = 0, . . . , 10. At cutoff 16384 the discrepancies were 4.49 × 10^{−10} and 1.81 × 10^{−11} for (h, x) = (−0.2, 0.13), (−0.125, 0.67). At the resonances (−0.5, 0.23) and (0.5, 0.37) they were 1.33×10^{−8} or less and 1.56×10^{−15} or less, respectively. The resonance values on the connection side were computed by taking a symmetric parameter limit at high precision. These quadratures are finite-cutoff numerical checks, not certified error bounds.

## 18. The transition to Gaussian moments at growing depth

Theorem 18.1 (simultaneous approach from the disk). Let d = 1 −z^{2}, c = Nd and z ↑ 1. For h on a compact subset of ℜh > −1 and s in a compact subset of ℂ, there are constants C, κ, c_{0} > 0 such that, for z sufficiently close to one and c ≥c_{0},

^{|||}d^{s2}T_{N}(h, s; z) − Γ(1 + h) _{ 1}F_{1}(−h; 1; −s^{2}z^{2})^{|||} ≤C(1 + d^{−(ℑs)2})e^{−κc}. (18.1)

Consequently every real tilt admits the transition for every c_{N} →∞ with z_{N} ↑ 1, including all microscopic inverse exponents in the ordinary domain. The binary header and implementation require little-endian signed 128-bit intermediates and a long-double significand of at least 64 bits on the tested GNU/IEEE platform.

A normalized butterfly averages two inputs with a unit exact twiddle, priced root and product errors and a dyadic half shift. Its error increases by at most 64U per stage at these bounded moduli. Execution scope and practical companion.

The preceding computation executes the bound construction, not all of the finite moments on a continuum. The rank-four common formula is intentionally conservative and long. A useful practical algorithm should select a much shorter input-dependent filter and then check its own source, image, arithmetic and readout errors. A proof that a finite formula has a uniform absolute error is not an unconditional finite-arithmetic relative guarantee.

The new terminal_hybrid.py implements the complementary pointwise selection. It exposes design(N,z,s, h,delta,cap,goal) and bound(N,z,h,s,delta,operation). The operation includes the actual filter, chart, population if any, and direction/spectral panel counts. Every proposed schedule is evaluated in outward arith-metic. Warm orders must call bound again; an incoming inverse-order allowance is not reused for a different order. The complete sampler must also reprice folded aliases and all other budgets. The native integration and its cold/warm receipts are recorded in the practical verification section; a terminal-design receipt alone is not an end-to-end certificate.

The design menu tests the signed-gap representation away from an exact wall and low-clipping core charts as well as the inherited charts. It rejects invalid contours rather than changing branches. If no candidate meets the target before the resource cap, it returns the best finite allowance with goal_met=false, or raises an explicit resource exception when none is valid. The full query’s absolute/relative status remains the final decision.

The core, signed-gap and folded terminal allowances already contain the Mellin multiplier. They are not multiplied by it twice. The finite image has its own coefficient, truncation, alias and arithmetic bounds. Likewise, the source angular allowance is for the physical determinant. The literal dyadic basis recovery of Proposition 5.8 applies to its computed arithmetic residual; it does not multiply the physical analytic source error again.

Every accepted input uses exact rational strings for z, ℜh, ℑh, ℜs, ℑs. Positive moduli use their real logarithms. The complex preparation is never normalized to a probability. At nonnegative integer order, the enclosed Taylor coefficient gives the result directly. Near such an order the deflated products of Theorem 21.21 avoid a numerical division by a pole. Warm noninteger queries recompute every order-dependent multiplier and error term.

Construction and reuse. The planner selects a finite convolution filter, admissible contour and resonant population, or a valid signed-gap bound. Its floating proposals are followed by outward checks. The alternative terminal_hybrid.py adds low-clipping contours and wider exact convolution filters; each saved operation records its representation, panels and parameters. A terminal goal is an allocation, not a certificate. A best finite bound that misses that allocation may still give a valid absolute result; its final modulus test decides whether the requested relative tolerance is met.

For each eligible integer stride, the reciprocal-support separation and the two folded costs are checked. Dense stride one is a fallback. The source is computed at the actual retained frequencies, with angular resolution selected from the prepared-symbol inequalities. The framed native determinant uses 104-bit fixed point and exports integer centres with their exact dyadic divisors; Arb handles 192/256-bit source, special-function and final contractions. These are the executed arithmetic settings, not a rank-uniform claim that this precision always suffices. A fresh Cauchy image, code hashes and source-row hashes complete the preparation. Every replay checks these hashes, the expected frequency sequence, the angular denominators and the absence of an omitted nonzero weight.

The cache binds (N, z, s), its numerical source and image, and the implementation that enclosed them. It does not bind the query order h. Its terminal filter stays fixed for warm orders, while the entire error budget is recomputed. Preparations from a different radius or tilt cannot be substituted. The original critical engine remains unchanged so its sealed receipts are replayable; the new gap/core engine has a separate seal. A partial interrupted source is not treated as a finished preparation. A mismatched cache returns an invalid- preparation outcome, rather than a numerical value with a certificate.

If a valid nonzero disk misses the relative tolerance, the selector can propose a smaller absolute allocation from its modulus lower bound and construct a separate order-adapted child preparation. This matters when a warm positive order amplifies the folded-alias allowance of an inverse-order guard. The new filter uses the actual query order; it is justified by the same identity and the ℜh > −1 tail and beta bounds. A new source and code seal prevents it from changing the meaning of an earlier cache. The final disk must again pass every error and modulus check. If the refinement is impossible within the cap, the already valid absolute disk is retained with the failed-refinement status.

Method selection. For N = 1, the exact hypergeometric identity avoids the historical crash. At N = 2, z = 0 the gamma formula is used only in the ordinary domain ℜh > −1/2; outside it the answer is divergent. At positive rank-two radius the inherited validated Duffy branch is retained, with its specified domain and resource tests. Rank three uses the new conditional source estimator on the tested critical interval [.25, .4], or the inherited certified s = −3 slice when applicable. An explicit rank3-wide option attempts 0 < z ≤.9 with further bounded refinements; it is an estimated extension, not a uniform theorem. Other low-rank and centre branches retain their predecessor status. At ranks four through eight below .82 the planner selects the new critical/gap construction; above it the earned exterior construction remains available. Theorem 21.25 proves a connected ideal-formula domain, while the actual adaptive query checks its own formula and can report a resource limit.

The rank-three estimator jointly refines the singular pair, spectator and regular-source grids, and compares a second exact partition. It monitors its absolute summation size and the proven omitted central contribution. Its eightfold refinement/roundoff allowance is an empirical estimator; it is never reported as an interval proof for

<!-- Source PDF page 322 -->

the complete quadrature. The low-rank tests below include a failure at the required tolerance and a concrete false-convergence example that justifies retaining the regular channel.

Statuses and accuracy. For an enclosed centre v and absolute radius E, relative accuracy is reported only when an outward lower bound for |v| −E is positive and E/(|v| −E) ≤ 10^{−10}. Otherwise a valid disk is reported as absolute-only, with a separate zero-possible flag. A zero-containing disk does not prove that its centre is a zero; the inherited zero-count theorem has a separate argument. These distinctions are implemented as follows.

The original target asks for an error estimate, so the estimated outcomes remain useful. They are not relabelled as failures merely because a stronger certificate is unavailable. Conversely, neither a source match nor a stable numerical value turns an estimate into a certificate. Cold time includes preparation; warm time includes source integrity and the new order contraction. The accompanying receipts record both, rather than counting a cached preparation as free for a first query.

## Implemented scalar readout and arithmetic contract (O9)

The entry point is odd_rank_investigation/odd.py. It accepts exact decimal or rational strings for z, the real and imaginary parts of h, and the independent parts of s. Its certified domain is N ∈{5, 7}, 0 ≤z ≤ 1/40, and the original complex box. The source cache is fixed at 2496 consecutive lattice indices with ∆= 8/25 and the exact filter K = 512, b = 32, p = 64. The last weight is zero; every preceding nonzero weight is retained. There is no decimated or frozen sparse prefix.

At positive radius the source adapter calls the unchanged HaarSpectral physical-source planner, witness and native kernel. Source bands use their actual preparation and direction dimensions, with target angular allowance −30 10 and preparation DFT ceiling 4096. The original complex Mellin image comes from the inherited coefficient and deflated readout engines. The small-radius physical restoration factor is proved to be one; the source is neither conjugated nor probability-normalized.

At the centre the source is exactly det[J_{j−k}(r)]^{N}_{j,k}^{−}_{=0}^{1}. Arb evaluates the determinant and checks its conversion to a −103 104-bit dyadic centre, with allowance 2 per sample. Its Taylor image coefficients are exact rationals from the inherited subset determinant. This avoids passing a fictitious positive translation frequency through the native header. The requested tilt remains in metadata, while the mathematical source is correctly tilt-independent.

| Engine | Executed precision or arithmetic |
| --- | --- |
| Positive-radius native source | 104-bit fixed point, explicit residual |
| Native preparation witness | 192-bit Arb/Acb |
| Inherited image evaluation | 256-bit Arb/Acb |
| Final contraction and printed centre | 384-bit Arb/Acb; 85 decimal digits |
| Centre determinant and rational image | 384-bit evaluation before checked encoding |
| Filter CDF and symbolic identities | Exact integer/rational arithmetic |
| Uniform inequalities | Separate 256- and 384-bit outward executions |

The final disk adds five individually nonnegative quantities: native finite arithmetic, finite angular/source ap-proximation, the complete Mellin image, the actual filtered terminal price, and ball accumulation plus decimal export. At exact orders h = 0, 1, 2, 3, the code extracts the corresponding image coefficient directly. At a nearby order it deflates the gamma–zeta product using the exact rational offset before interval multiplication. No error allowance from an unexecuted common grid is borrowed.

For centre c and total absolute allowance E, the relative gate uses m ≤|c| −E. Only when m > 0 and low low −10 E/m < 10 does the result receive a relative certificate. Otherwise a valid absolute disk remains an absolute low result. A requested input outside the exact native rational header is refused without rounding its physical radius.

Raw executions retain their original CANDIDATE status. The separate certification ledger checks each physical input, its producing code and source bytes, all error components, the terminal resources and the lower-modulus test. The public interface requires a final mathematical and source audit manifest. Certified reuse of an existing cache requires its preparation hash to be an approved executed cache; a newly generated source can be used in the same verified execution. ## Executable evaluator and finite-arithmetic contract (E10)

The reviewed public entry point is even_rank_investigation/even.py. It accepts exact rational physical inputs, covers N = 4, 6, 8 and 0 ≤z ≤ 1/40, and returns a complex disk, a full component budget, source provenance, and a recomputed modulus classification. Existing source caches require reviewed generation provenance for a certified result. A fresh cache may be generated during the verified run. Explicit candidate mode never issues a certified status. Receipts are created exclusively and are kept outside the source-cache directory.

For a final centre c and absolute error E, the modulus floor and relative bound are

ℓ = |c| −E, ε = E/ℓ (ℓ> 0). lower rel

The status is CERTIFIED_RELATIVE only if this recomputed upper bound is strictly below 10^{−10}. Other-wise the valid result is CERTIFIED_ABSOLUTE; a disk containing zero cannot earn a relative claim. An unsupported source or input is refused rather than assigned an estimated certificate.

The positive-radius native source uses the unchanged 104-bit fixed-point engine, 192-bit preparation witnesses and 256-bit image generation. Actual scalar contractions and new rank-four coefficients use 384-bit Arb/Acb in the main matrix. At the centre the determinant is generated with Arb and checked before dyadic encoding, and image coefficients are exact rational data. The displayed final precision does not increase the precision of an existing cache. Source, angular and image errors remain separate from the final ball radius. Positive-source compilation disables fast-math and floating contraction.

The original untranslated signed-direction projection is retained, followed by its exact translation Bessel contrac-tion. A trapezoid applied after translation would require a different alias bound and is not substituted. The native positive-frequency rational header remains signed-32-bit; unsupported exact numerators or denominators are explicitly refused. No physical radius is rounded.

Two more preparations at .02 use s = −2.4 + 1.8i and s = 3i. Rank four stores 2048 consecutive source rows; ranks six and eight store 4096. Positive sources use the actual Fourier

Reusing the coefficients makes scalar contractions much cheaper. The public interface selects 8 ≤L ≤ 24 using the proved complete preparation return at the requested input, and recomputes every resulting budget. ## 22. Verification and limits of the results

The scripts distinguish a numerical comparison from an enclosure with a proved error bound. The rank-two determinant derivation is checked at integer, noninteger and resonant exponents. The interior large-size checks evaluate a finite Toeplitz determinant and its radial integral against the limiting Kummer expression. The depth scripts compare the 1/N correction with the exact confluent determinant and compare the microscopic projection covariance with an independently evaluated finite moment. At N = 384, m = 2, j = 1, c = 1.3, the first-order corrected normalized value differs from the exact formula by approximately 9.17 × 10^{−7}; halving the mesh 1/N

<!-- Source PDF page 387 -->

divides the error by approximately four. These samples test the derivations. The estimates in the text supply their proofs.

At the centre, rank three has a separate difference equation tested against exact trace moments. The executable interval evaluator includes exact rational input conventions, outward-rounded complex arithmetic and a separate relative-error status. Rank one covers independent h, s. The rank-two centre requires ℜh > −1/2. Its interior diagonal branch covers 0 < z < 1, s = h, ℜh > −1, including the logarithmic resonances. At N = 2, z = 0.9, h = s = 0.6 + 0.2i the exact-endpoint export certifies relative radius below 6.5 × 10^{−36}. An independent high-precision Haar integral lies inside. A second high-precision test checks a logarithmic resonance. ## Verification of the full-state propagation

The named higher-rank radius source comprised 129 pages. Its editable text matched the companion archive byte for byte. All 250 entries of the predecessor manifest were checked and all 92 mathematical verification programs were rerun, including the inverse-order four-state crossing, rank-two controls, integer-moment tests, and the rank-four floating-point failure. The earlier special crossing uses h = −1/4, s = −3. The present 20- and 35-state runs use distinct parameters and distinct initial integrals.

The new exact checks are the degree-bounded generator identities, the rank-three residue identity, the rank-four Laurent identities and shear, and the coefficient constructions. The interval checks are the separate incoming source enclosures, the nonvanishing denominators on the complex paths, the polynomial defects and inverse bounds, the physical phase combination, the end-condition checks, and the continuous lower-modulus cover for the separate scalar evaluator. The raw files contain rectangular real and imaginary enclosures as well as scalar disk budgets. A disk about an unshortened centre may be narrower than the radius obtained by circumscribing its displayed componentwise rectangle. The standalone verification records give the exact rational parameters, the component order, precision, truncation, branch signs and endpoint definitions.

The following comparisons have a different evidential status. Angular grids and centered differences compare independent implementations of the physical reduction. They have no certified integration remainder. The floating-point minimization of a representative scalar row only proposes dyadic coefficients. Its eventual error bound uses exact annihilation on the physical solution and interval norms of the proposed row. Overlap between independent enclosures checks consistency; each construction supplies its own inclusion proof. The derivatives of the preparation and the Weyl normalization enter both the physical definition and the error analysis. Removing them makes the specified control intervals disjoint. The raw source, scripts and preserved research note accompany this edition.

Two restricted extensions are reproducible from the new material. At rank three the order-jet calculation propa-gates 40 coordinates and evaluates the derivative connection at a zero of the cosine. At the two regular outgoing radii the scalar table has a verified lower modulus across each continuous parameter set. These have distinct sources of accuracy: a full path proof at the chosen points, and direct original-Haar integration for the continu-ous sets. The new parameter disks and rank-four exceptional calculation are given in Theorems 10.15–10.17 and 21.12. Consecutive critical crossings with a shared uniform budget and full-path validation of smaller moving charts remain open.

On a failed budget it refines the angular input and tests it with the already enclosed path matrices before increasing the path precision. The comparison here uses T_{N} as defined in Section 1. A rigorous radius is a stronger result than a refinement estimate. The status at N = 2, z = 0, ℜh ≤−1/2 is divergent. A relative error is undefined at a zero.

The complete predecessor release contained 2,791 checksummed members. All entries were verified against their actual bytes. Its 35-component rank-four and 56-component rank-five receipt checks were replayed. The three rank-four reference runs using 12, 16 and 56 order pairs retain their unexecuted status. The order-disk and tilt-disk statements at rank five keep their separate fixed parameters. The current high-rank lattice results reconstruct the scalar at a queried real radius. The exact cubic-symbol and finite-rank complex-circle checks were repeated in this edition; they test those coefficients and normalizations. They do not furnish a fresh proof of the arbitrary-order or simultaneous-limit estimates.

The original fitted-tail executable and its two detailed comparison maps were absent. Its roughly 3,300 and 1,850 reference-point counts remain producer reports. The saved successor algorithms are available. Fourteen inherited low-rank tests were run before interpreting the changes. The general low-rank comparison matrix records 27 comparisons, including one out-of-box diagonal control. Ten returned certified relative accuracy, fifteen estimated relative accuracy, one a certified absolute-only result, and one a divergent status. Three adaptive two-angle Arb evaluations separately attained relative bounds below 1.667 × 10^{−11}. The N = 1, z = 0.7 programme example works in the shipped rank-one branch. The interval checks in Section 8 cover arbitrarily small positive input radii on the specified rank-two order strip.

The general finite-rank suite contains 32 core runs and seven stress runs before individual repairs or refinements. It includes a separately enclosed complex mass, the rank-four physical transfer where applicable, independent original-angle Fourier calculations, and independently calculated integer mass and diagonal benchmarks at ranks three through eight. Resource caps remain part of each reported status. A histogram of passes cannot certify a parameter continuum. The centre and z = 10^{−32} inverse cases at ranks three and four exceeded the requested estimated tolerance in the fast core suite. The centre, tilt-transfer and response branches now enclose all four, including every tilt on the rank-four disk of Theorem 9.5 at the indicated fixed order. The signed-wave repair at rank three targets the slow detuning frequency at z = 1/3+10^{−5}; neglecting it gave a substantial change between cutoffs. At the original corner (N, z, h, s) = (5, 0.9, 3+3i, 3) the first binary64 run returned an estimated relative −9 error 1.92 × 10. Computing the sensitive small-frequency part at wider precision returned approximately −22.32418966361 + 37.89957762365i with estimated relative error 1.54 × 10^{−11}. The direct five-angle Weyl grid in the verification package sums over ordered subsets of distinct nodes using symmetry; all repeated-node terms vanish. Changing the common grid rotation tests angular aliasing. This is an independent numerical comparison. The separate whole-range original-angle calculation agrees with the repaired result to 5.29 × 10^{−13} relative. On a 160-node Weyl grid at a quarter-step shift the five-angle sum gives −22.3241896635986 + 37.8995776236368i. Its successive grid differences have no claimed rigorous rate.

The source-level controls at N = 7, 8 include the original single-eigenangle Fourier integral with an independently bounded trapezoidal rule at zero, three nonzero real frequencies, and r = 1.5 + 0.75i. At all ten inputs the original and transformed enclosures intersect; all eight nonzero inputs exclude the result obtained by dropping translation. The radial samples and their tails are bounded separately in Proposition 21.15. The table above and accompanying receipts record each full radial calculation, enclosure and independent comparison.

At the two inverse-region endpoints an independent calculation used the untransformed one-angle Weyl symbol and continuous radial Gauss integration. At cutoffs 12, 24, 40 and 64 it successively approached the enclosed values. The fine-rule absolute discrepancies at cutoff 64 were below 1.84 × 10^{−16} at both ranks. A coarser rank-eight rule gave a relative discrepancy near 4.46 × 10^{−10} even when the last two cutoffs agreed. Radial refinement alone would have concealed this quadrature error.

The limiting obstacle at the upper-radius, inverse-order corner is quantitative. Angular Fourier decay slows as the preparation poles move toward the integration circle, the inverse Mellin weight decays slowly, and a crude absolute contour estimate retains little of the balanced-saddle cancellation. The new calculations make each of those errors separately measurable. A finite-rank implementation with verified accuracy and practical cost throughout the original nonzero, integrable box remains open.

Across 68 repeat-order checks of the dense caches, 61 returned relative certificates and seven returned absolute-only certificates. The change of resonant population in Corollary 5.13 also covered consecutive walls. The rank-six and rank-eight executions there test the two- and three-agreeing-sign cores at physical noninteger orders. That edition left open how much of the original inverse-order and tilt box admits practical bounds throughout these connected radial intervals; Theorems 21.24–21.25 and Corollary 21.26 and the new computations below address this question without asserting uniform relative accuracy. At small rank the algebraic tail from the central population becomes less integrable as the order approaches −.95. Quantifying that loss before enlarging a radial interval would address a current gap in the evaluator. The four asymptotic regimes and the open identification of the displayed rank-three elliptic expression retain their predecessor qualifications.

## Independent and adversarial verification of the critical continuation

The new certificate engine and the checking calculations share the physical Haar observable and the Weyl–Andreief identity. Their reference preparation, radial quadrature and scalar contraction are separately implemented. This is useful independence of representations and code, not an assertion that they have no common mathematical premise.

The recovered missing-mass correction was replayed at 192 bits. The old inverse formula’s repaired exact-arithmetic allowance is less than 2.871948101 · 10^{−17}, with the preparation mass included in the uniform image tail. A complete cold rank-six source at its second wall was also rebuilt; it reproduced the inherited midpoint and relative allowance 5.228498525 · 10^{−14}. These receipts are current executions, whereas other inherited receipts remain producer reports unless individually marked. Neither replay audits the microscopic or circle-limit proofs.

The checker verified the Mehta constants by independent Gaussian Hankel determinants at ranks zero through eight, compared finite-rank integer moments using original-angle bivariate Toeplitz determinants, and checked the first two signed-saddle coefficients against exact Bessel expansions. The additional rank-three coefficient calculation is stated separately. Each is tested at its actual scope; an integer check does not certify a noninteger tail.

The native radius includes its source, alias, terminal, image, arithmetic and readout allowances. The independent reference has an estimated, not certified, combined error.

Controls that change the actual calculation

For the sparse rank-four critical preparation at z = .5, h = −.95 + .77i, s = −.7 + 1.13i, the certified absolute allowance is 1.009 · 10^{−11}. The following controls reuse the same physical source rows and change the stated contraction only:

All controls are returned with an explicit noncertificate status. Their inherited allowance is not valid for the altered formula. The displacements exceed the correct disk by large margins and distinguish the required nor-malization and folded-lattice recovery from plausible-looking incomplete contractions.

At the same radius, stride three has a positive reciprocal-support gap and its guard filter has a proved alias allowance below 2.18 · 10^{−35}. Stride four fails the separation test and is rejected before a certificate is returned. A disposable copied cache with modified parameter bytes is rejected by the integrity gate; the saved cache itself is not changed. Synthetic readout tests return absolute-only status for a zero-containing disk and for inadequate

<!-- Source PDF page 404 -->

relative precision, and reject nonfinite or negative error components. Synthetic gate tests are not physical Haar evaluations.

An independent logarithm control at s = 3i replaces the real log |Λ|^{2} by log |Λ|^{2} + 2πi. It multiplies the prepa- −6π ration by e, changing the displayed moment by more than .0397. This is a changed observable, not another permissible branch of the ordinary expectation. The physical calculation always uses real logarithms of positive moduli.

The rank-three source implementation retains its own particularly useful failed control: fixing the regular-source angular grid at eight nodes while refining the other two quadratures gives successive values differing by only −14 −4 1.58·10, despite an error about 9.81·10. This directly motivates joint refinement and the alternate-partition check; an apparent radial convergence test alone is inadequate.

What the checks do not establish

The finite comparisons do not prove coverage of the full parameter box. The connected-region claims instead depend on their complete closed-cell interval cover and analytic order/tilt majorants. The uniform finite formula still needs input-specific finite-arithmetic and nonzero-modulus gates. No scalar result is full-state multiwall transport. No rigorous numerical constant for the full paired stationary-phase remainder has been obtained, and the general rank-three adaptive method remains estimated. Near zeros, a small absolute allowance does not imply a relative guarantee.

The checker also inspected the new connected terminal selector and its join to the earlier pointwise engine. The two terminal methods bound the same omitted fine-grid scalar sum, and the complete term is recomputed at each warm order. The implementation and seals are separate from the frozen earlier sparse code. For a regional gap cell, upper-radius preparation/support factors and lower-radius direction damping are both retained. The real-source and direction approximations are uniform in real frequency: their exact Bessel contraction uses coefficients of modulus at most one even at high frequency. Consequently extending the last index changes the finite-source bound by the explicitly priced sum of absolute weights, rather than silently requiring a new angular frequency theorem. The join to the exterior interval at .82 is a piecewise family of scalar formulas with the maximum of the two bounds; it is not one unchanged filter or a differential connection carrying hidden state.

Reproduction scripts are final_controls.py, fresh_references.py, fresh_lowrank_reference.py, final_comparison.py, rank3_saddle_cubic.py, fresh_small_reference.py and rank3_third_correction.py. The machine-readable receipts retain exact inputs, implementation hashes, source dependency hashes, numerical status and actual costs. positive_repair_reference.py records the additional positive-order comparison. Nine public-interface smoke checks also passed, including all three sealed engines, the positive-order child, two physical-preparation transplant rejections, a resource cap, divergence and the zero-containing case. These are warm replays and status checks, not fresh source integrations.

final_comparison.py recomputes differences from receipts; it does not represent itself as rerunning their source calculations.

The release was also tested from a fresh staged folder containing only the selected runtime sources, with depen-dency roots checked explicitly. From a different current directory, it rebuilt the N = 5, z = .02 complex inverse query in 3.95 s, then evaluated a different positive complex order in .534 s. The source was newly generated. This verifies the recorded executable paths and statuses, not the entire selector or a uniform cost bound. A separate read-only accounting audit replayed all 423 radius cells at 256 bits, including the population labels at all eleven positive critical radii; it found no accounting mismatch.

## Rank-three source evaluation: executed scope and failure controls

The rank-three implementation is a scalar source quadrature. It does not continue a full differential state. The identity and the conditional integrability statements preceding it are proved. The numerical stopping rule estimates the error; it does not enclose the full cubature remainder.

adaptive_rank3.py is the frozen critical-interval routine. It attempts 1/4 ≤z ≤ 2/5, successively refines the conditional pair and outer-angle rules and the separate regular-source grid, and changes the exact partition from K = 4 to K = 5 before accepting. A conservative absolute-sum term monitors binary64 cancellation.

These are replays of an inherited certified method, rather than a new rank-two theorem.

The strongest next step for rank three is a validated joint quadrature remainder that preserves the pair repulsion and the regular partition channel. The exact endpoint and cutoff bounds now control the central chart, but they do not yet bound every quadrature and finite-arithmetic error. The v2 range remains opt-in, and no rank-three whole-box accuracy claim is made.

## Coverage ledger and the next mathematical obligation

The original specification seeks 10^{−10} relative accuracy with an error estimate on 1 ≤ N ≤ 8, 0 ≤ z ≤ .9, −.95 ≤ℜh ≤ 3, |ℑh| ≤ 3, |s| ≤ 3, wherever the ordinary expectation exists and relative accuracy is meaningful. The whole specification is not yet met. The following ledger separates the mathematical domains from the evidence of actual evaluation. A pointwise certificate can be stronger than a general error estimate without proving uniform cost or universal success.

without the actual external expression and definitions. The separate research note remains unchanged for restora-tion of complete provenance before publication.

Why the next step is lower-rank error control. The present source method already crosses the physical critical radii without needing a larger transported differential state. The most direct remaining improvements are (i) a usable remainder bound for the paired saddle expansion, retaining the detuning ω = Nz +2m−N instead of dividing by it, and (ii) validated joint quadrature for the rank-three partition. Proposition 3.3 supplies a concrete additional coefficient, and Corollary 4.6 supplies a useful uniform near-centre component. Neither alone bounds the rest of the quadrature or its arithmetic. These are precise missing estimates. Further repeated-wall full-state transport is a separate worthwhile objective when the full state is required, but the current evidence does not make it a prerequisite for improving the scalar evaluator target.

## Remaining mathematical and numerical questions

At fixed positive depth the real-tilt threshold is sharp. For fixed s = u + iv with v ̸= 0, the total variation on the original unitary ensemble after complex mass scaling is

```text
|N^{−s2}| Z_{N}(u, z_{N}) ∼N^{v2}A_{u}(c).
```

Theorem 16.4 proves weighted variation convergence after taking the planar mark at fixed positive depth. Its constants depend on compact depth and tilt ranges and on the order of the expansion. Thus the cancellation on the mark plane resolves the fixed-depth issue even for independent complex exponents. The zero sets in Corollary 16.5 have not been located explicitly.

Theorems 18.2 and 19.10 give the two moving-depth limits for independent complex parameters in their stated domains. Proposition 19.12 resolves the leading transverse scale and its rare excursions. Theorems 19.14–19.15 give a uniform first correction on the transverse-to-off-line overlap for bounded longitudinal coordinate. The_{√√} compact interior of the sector |J|/ B < 2 has its own two-term expansion. A pointwise approximation uniform through its one-angle front and a pointwise planar resolution around λQ = 1 remain open. Proposition 19.19 identifies the locally finite limiting measure in the latter window. Proposition 19.16 treats the first cutoff for the marginal tail. Its other threshold boundaries and the transition between adjacent planar bands in Proposition 19.17 require further analysis. The arguments give locally uniform constants on parameter compacts; effective numerical constants for the asymptotic comparison and estimates uniform at unbounded imaginary parameters remain to be developed.

Proposition 10.4 constructs planar equations for independently noninteger (h, s) at any rank. Theorem 10.5 supplies ordinary equations on regular intervals for every rank N ≥ 2. Theorem 10.6 reduces the state dimension and Theorem 10.9 specifies the exact physical connection at every interior critical trace radius. The full 20- and 35-coordinate path matrices now have rigorous error bounds for the crossings of Proposition 21.9. Rank-uniform precision and cost bounds for long or multiple crossings remain open. Theorem 10.17 resolves the selected rank-four singular column and its scalar projection at the stated exceptional parameters. Section 23 resolves the normal-jet scalar projection at ranks three and four via Theorem 23.1’s shortcut and at every rank N ≥ 3 off (10.9) via Theorem 23.1A, and gives an independent physical calculation at intersecting divisors. Section 24 develops one-pair variable-order rank-four transport across the wall z = 1/2, and Section 25 executes noninteger rank-five two-wall transport on s = −5 and |s+5| ≤ 1/16; additional indicial collisions in sheared full-state charts, excluded radii in (10.9), and efficient arbitrary-tilt or general-rank multiwall transport remain open. Large group-inverse powers, a near-resonant readout and loss of compatible digits can dominate the reduction. The bounds of Theorem 21.5 and the individual certificates in this edition give independent scalar checkpoints. They leave open a practical uniform inverse-order evaluator over the wider target. At rank two the adaptive evaluator attains the stated relative accuracy throughout the exact-rational points of the closed region of Theorem 21.4. Additional branches provide pointwise certificates. For the wider target 1 ≤N ≤ 8, 0 ≤z ≤ 0.9, −0.95 ≤ℜh ≤ 3, |ℑh| ≤ 3, |s| ≤ 3, divergent cases require exclusion, and relative error is undefined at a complex zero. Uniform resource bounds and broad independent higher-rank reference values for admissible noninteger inputs remain to be established.

## Independent checks, failures, and repairs (R8)

The finite Laurent source was evaluated independently by its direct finite Fourier/Bessel determinant, using 256-bit Acb Bessel calls. Four checks covered the critical generic tilt, the quarter-radius corner, the upper radius endpoint and the exact s = −3 slice. All differences lie inside the proved remainder. On s = −3, the resonant −4 −6 2 2 r and r coefficients enclose respectively 4𝒫_{s}/π and −3𝒫_{s}/π, as required by inherited Proposition 3.3.

The finite original-source engine was also checked against the independent identity

Φ(r) = d^{−9}J_{0}(ar)[J_{0}(r)^{3} + 2J_{0}(r)J_{1}(r)^{2} + 2J_{1}(r)^{2}J_{2}(r) −J_{0}(r)J_{2}(r)^{2}] (s = −3).

Forty retained lattice samples lay inside the finite-source enclosures. Independent original-angle Toeplitz/hypergeometric mass checks validate the complex preparation at h = 0. The elementary identities T_{3}(0, 0; z) = 1 and 6 T (1, 0; z) = 1 −z test normalization and integer-order cancellation. The latter was independently obtained 3 from the mixed coefficient of an original-Haar Toeplitz determinant.

Extended-precision conditional calculations provide a different numerical readout. They use actual 64-significand-bit long double arithmetic, corrected quadrature nodes and weights, stable local geometry, and compensated accumulation. The hard quarter input now meets its estimated target; the left, critical and right checks also meet their estimated targets. Their entire moments remain estimated, because their complementary conditional quadrature has no complete rigorous remainder. The whole-source certificates do not depend on their agreement.

Independent comparisons support the implementation but do not replace the analytic proof of the remainder.

The following failures remain preserved rather than overwritten:

1. The first Bessel coefficient aggregation multiplied a chosen sign placement by a binomial multiplicity after

permutation reduction. An independent exact-source comparison caught it. All eight placements are now explicitly summed. Superseded coefficients are labelled in the route-A records.

2. Direct large-shift Lerch evaluation produced unusably wide balls. A subsequent repeated phase recurrence

also produced a very large valid enclosure through interval wrapping. The successful implementation uses (R7.1), higher precision and independent phases.

<!-- Source PDF page 412 -->

3. The exact h = 1 test initially refused a valid result because a nonnegative absolute-value interval containing

zero was stored by Arb as a symmetric ball. Testing that representation for a nonnegative lower endpoint was too strict. Taking its rigorous absolute upper endpoint repaired the guard; the rerun encloses the exact value 728/729.

4. An exact near-critical radius with a denominator exceeding the inherited signed 32-bit header failed be-

fore source evaluation. The failure is retained. The executed neighboring tests use exact radii 1/3 ± 1/3000000000, whose frequency steps fit the ABI. Requested parameters are never silently rounded.

5. A regular-channel prototype generated a nonfinite ball by applying a generic power operation to an interval

straddling zero. Direct interval multiplication and explicit finiteness checks repaired it. Its failed receipt and large-error coarse-grid control remain separate.

6. Higher precision did not cure false convergence: with the regular grid frozen at eight nodes, conditional

48- versus 64-point results agreed to 6.65064 10^{−16} while retaining a bias of 9.810125 10^{−4} against joint refinement.

7. An independent expensive conditional test at the largest imaginary order was stopped during refinement

after the useful completed checks. Its partial record is labelled unfinished; the corresponding whole-source input was independently enclosed by the new route.

Costs and conditioning

Nine sealed preparations contain 204800 executed native samples and about 16.9 MB of data. The positive generic z = .9 source used K = 98304 and took about 166 seconds with two workers under shared load. The independent negative generic tilt used K = 65536 and took about 109 seconds. Their exact physical restoration factors are respectively 256 and 262144. The inherited 104-bit fixed-point kernel passed every executed guard. It was not replaced merely because a conservative asymptotic bound worsened.

The endpoint positive-order example has modulus near .054 and its native allowance is about 5.407 10^{−15}. It therefore provides a useful smaller complex readout challenge. Coefficient preparation is a substantial cold-run cost; source and tail caches are reusable across orders at fixed radius and tilt. Warm contraction still prices every rounding operation and every source row. The report’s timings describe actual executions, not a uniform runtime guarantee.

Independent algebra and scalar checks

The exact filter agrees with a separately implemented bounded-composition inclusion–exclusion formula at all 2498 tested indices. Three scalar reconstructions use reflected gamma factors and reversed summation order; their independently accounted budgets agree. The old/new positive-radius comparisons share the native source and image engines; agreement of those readouts alone is therefore not an independent source verification. The original-circle source and integer checks supply that separate challenge. Each comparison records its shared dependencies.

Controls that deliberately failed

Unbudgeted conversion of certified source centres to IEEE double precision was rejected in all three scalar controls: discrepancies of order 4 10^{−18} to 10^{−17} exceed the corresponding declared fine enclosures. This directly detects false precision even when printed digits appear stable. Incorrect cutoff endpoints and inappropriate population aggregation are also retained as adversarial controls.

The first domain guards compared Arb balls with exact boundary values and incorrectly refused ℜh = −.95 or |s| = 3. Membership is now decided in exact rational arithmetic before ball conversion. An independent mass audit originally required a strict inequality when both exact discrepancy and allowance were zero; its zero-equality case was repaired and the earlier failure record retained. The public-interface audit also identified overstated centre precision on a reused cache and insufficient proof of origin for a self-rehashed cache. The generating metadata and approved cache provenance gates repair these issues without changing the mathematical core. Earlier source versions and refusal receipts remain available; none is relabelled as a successful certificate.

## Failed controls, repairs and remaining limitations (E12)

The decisive frozen-prefix failure

At N = 4, z = 0, h = −.95, contraction of the same finite prefix at 384 and 512 bits agrees to within 9.61 10^{−99}. Nevertheless, omitting the complete tail changes the scalar by more than 3.8003401 10^{−5}. The complete balanced polynomial alone contributes more than 3.8003322 10^{−5}, while the complete scalar error is below 1.179401 10^{−25}. This executed control decisively separates arithmetic stability from correctness of the physical readout.

The zero-frequency balanced phase also remains zero at directions with cos ϕ = 0 at positive radius. Six exact controls reject the proposed positive odd-rank gap for that population. Absolute summability or the explicit balanced kernel is essential; changing precision cannot create the missing frequency gap.

Preserved failed attempts and repairs

The first independent scalar-composition audit used a large-shift Acb Lerch reference whose ball radius was enormous. Its noninteger overlap labels were vacuous and have been explicitly withdrawn, with the original receipt preserved. The replacement uses polylogarithm minus a finite prefix, requires an informative reference radius, and rejects a factor-two error. It does not use the withdrawn comparisons as evidence.

<!-- Source PDF page 425 -->

An initial original-integer audit omitted the cached image coefficient’s ball radius from its comparison. The repaired audit includes that radius; the prior source and failure record remain preserved. An interval endpoint guard in an early contour component audit was likewise corrected without changing the underlying contour theorem. A preflight certificate builder initially recorded audit hashes without requiring each audit’s successful status and producer binding; the final builder checks both, as well as global before/after source snapshots. The public scalar assessor also requires the integer route to agree with the exact input order. No such preflight was promoted as a final certificate.

Earlier inherited adversarial controls for wrong sign aggregation, rectangular phase wrapping, fixed-grid false con-vergence, missing complex preparation, inadequate native arithmetic, unsupported rational headers and gamma– zeta cancellation remain in their original packages and the new provenance record.

What is still open

The connected theorem supplies absolute approximations throughout the box; it does not prove a uniform positive modulus. Successful samples cannot rule out complex zeros. The finite-arithmetic certificates apply to recorded inputs and resources, and the public central interface may require more resources or return only an absolute disk at a different input. No broad performance guarantee is inferred from this finite matrix.

The rank-eight positive-order examples are dominated by finite-source arithmetic, despite the much smaller an-alytic central theorem. Increasing the tail expansion cannot repair that arithmetic limitation. The rank-six uniform central bound is dominated by the absolute contour tail; input-specific pricing is substantially sharper. The new public interface is central only. Full-radius operation still requires dispatch to the inherited interior con-structions, whose larger common resources and arithmetic conditioning are not eliminated by the mathematical join.

Ranks one and two retain their distinct ordinary-moment domains. In particular, the rank-two centre requires ℜh > −1/2; an analytically continued value outside that domain is not an ordinary expectation. The fixed-interior, microscopic, shrinking-depth and circle regimes remain part of the ultimate programme and have not been re-proved or narrowed here.

At m = t = 3, ∆= 8/25, this is exactly 836849212.646484375. Twenty-eight outward checks verify the identity in its implemented use. The finite source is therefore contracted with a very large factor before cancellation against the image. The measured prefix–image cancellation ratios are approximately 8.72·10^{8} at z = 0.025 and 9.22·10^{9} at z = 0.9. These ratios diagnose conditioning; they are not used as error estimates.

At N = 8, z = 1/40 with the same h, s, the old source arithmetic costs about 2.998 · 10^{−14}, of which more than 99.45 percent comes from the first row. At the upper input, 128-bit HP2 for the first forty rows already gives relative error below 3.050 · 10^{−12} with the old image. The 192-bit first-forty source takes about 7.93 seconds on this run; the 128-bit version takes about 6.95 seconds. These are observed timings on a shared host, not uniform performance guarantees. The public default is 192 bits, with adaptive row count and image resources; no global optimum over bit counts is claimed.

Actual adaptive public runs

With a requested relative target 10^{−14}, the public selector starts from the reviewed inherited cache, observes source arithmetic dominance, and selects twelve replacement rows from the actual inherited suffix sum. It then sees image dominance and regenerates the Mellin image. The complete three-stage calculation reaches

E < 2.007 · 10^{−14}, E/ℓ< 4.606 · 10^{−16}.

The tighter twelve-row run takes about 8.76 seconds. At the central input, a requested −26 −28 −29 relative target 10 selects 47 rows and obtains E < 1.113 · 10 and relative error below 5.955 · 10. The actual selected rows, source precision and image precision are disclosed.

A resource selector is permitted to stop before exhausting the available mathematical precision. Its target is the user’s tolerance, with a defensible disk. If a later proposal worsens the bound, the earlier valid disk is kept. If the source arithmetic dominates, increasing asymptotic order is not a remedy. If the terminal dominates after the arithmetic repair, the next obligation is a new terminal/filter budget.

Preserved failures and repairs

The inherited sign aggregation, Vandermonde, phase wrapping, complex tilt, normalization, false-convergence, rational-header and near-integer controls remain unchanged. The new investigation adds the following concrete tests.

1. A fully consistent rehash of forged rank-four tail coefficients changes the scalar by more than 3.80034·10^{−5}

while two claimed small disks have summed radii below 2.359 · 10^{−25}. This demonstrates why structural hash consistency alone cannot confer mathematical origin. The public gate now rejects such an external tail without reviewed generation provenance.

2. Near a strict tolerance boundary, a pre-serialization comparison could pass while the outward displayed

relative bound fails. Classification is now performed on the serialized exact upper bound itself.

3. The backend must identify a successful refined source rather than the original parent directory. It must

also reproduce the exact old image centre consumed by that producer before replacing it. Sparse and dense inherited image contractors are algebraically related but have different finite centres. Dispatch v2 preserves v1 bytes and records an unchanged-branch bridge for the 75 earlier runs.

4. Increasing the image to J = 108 with H = 3 at N = 3, z = 0.025, h = 3 − 3i, s = 2.4 + 1.8i worsens its

arithmetic radius to about 0.28436, despite an unchanged printed centre. The systematic coefficient error is tiny; high-degree weights amplify finite coefficient noise. Keeping J = 108, m = 216 and changing the actual Cauchy radius to H = 6 reduces that image allowance below 2.694·10^{−41}, restoring a complete error below 1.131 · 10^{−18}. This explicit failure rules out indiscriminate image term growth as a universal policy.

5. Actual near-zero capped and adaptive runs verify absolute/relative classification. Injected scheduling time-

## Verification, failures, and evidence classifications (Z12)

The verification chain distinguishes six kinds of evidence:

1. Analytic identities and theorems, including source transformations, holomorphy, transport, Cauchy aliases,

and the implication from a common derivative cone to a modulus factor.

2. Executed outward inequalities, including M < 6, the local derivative constants, the strict Rouché slack,

and the rational floor 1/400.

3. Complete finite-arithmetic scalar, zero and derivative disks, admitted only with their exact physical inputs,

source generation and composed error contracts.

4. Numerical proposals such as a filter search or Newton predictor, which select candidates but prove no error

estimate or zero existence.

5. Reproductions using a shared source/readout engine, which test provenance and arithmetic composition

without being an independent original-source derivation.

6. Independent constructions, including original-Haar angular versus hypergeometric h=0 derivatives and the

direct reconstruction of analytic bounds, aliases, geometry and derivative components.

<!-- Source PDF page 430 -->

The independent analytic audit checks the exact common-rotation degree, Hölder and Schur exponents, Riesz coefficient, Jacobians, moving-mark regularity, and the differentiated preparation term. The transport audit reconstructs the selected 384-bit bounds and checks the exact second-moment series symbolically. The Cauchy audits reconstruct all phases, node displacements, scalar-error sums and folded aliases, including the degree-60 extension. The geometry audit independently executes the uniform comparison at 768 bits without calling its producer. The derivative audit independently rebuilds all eight root slope disks and the true-zero anchor.

There is also an independent challenge at an actually executed noninteger zero preparation, rather than only at the h=0 anchor. For the h = 0.001 root source, an Acb reconstruction of the finite projection checks physical rows 1, 8 and 40 using its own DFT, Bessel and determinant contraction. Separately, an original-Haar eigenvalue-circle calculation checks the first physical source sample with 4096 eigenangle nodes, 256 direction nodes, and explicit strip errors. Its discrepancy from the native physical centre is less than 8.183×10^{−30}, while the complete comparison allowance is below 2.812 × 10^{−22}. The actual directed gap-versus-allowance comparison passes. The independent circle’s own analytic error is below 8.731 × 10^{−82}. These checks use neither the native witness nor the fixed-point determinant arithmetic. They are independent sample checks with their own priced errors, not a second complete scalar zero proof.

The failure information is mathematically useful and is preserved:

• A pointwise supremum of the transformed preparation is too large for useful h continuation; original-Haar

rotation and a correlated Schur mass replace it without changing the source.

• A crude radius majorant is valid but ineffective. Anchored inverse transport and the exact second mark

moment reduce the local first-radius bound to below 196. This is a bound repair, not evidence of a physical singularity in the old representation.

• The first terminal filter is insufficient for accurate small-order coefficients. Appending physical rows and

repricing a stronger finite filter repairs the terminal component. Raising readout precision alone would not do so.

• The a = 2 halo does not justify M = 6. The actual proof uses the independently audited a = 11/4 receipt.

• A nonzero derivative modulus alone does not justify the modulus factor. The fixed complex derivative cone

is retained before integrating along the tilt segment.

• A Newton sequence, a scalar disk containing zero, or matching printed values does not certify a root. The

uniform zero theorem and a complete physical residual do.

• The sparse prefix improvement can be negligible at deep inverse order. Both that adverse resource result

and the stride-two adversarial control remain part of the verification package.

Inherited adversarial controls remain dependencies of the broader programme: incorrect saddle aggregation, omitted Vandermonde zeros, complex-tilt conjugation, native-to-physical normalization errors, interval phase wrapping, frozen-grid false convergence, missing balanced terminals, inadequate source precision, unsupported exact headers, near-integer gamma–zeta cancellation, unreviewed caches, and zero-containing relative disks. This construction does not relabel every inherited control as a newly executed test. Its new checks address the continuation, derivative, source-lineage, sparse-alias, and modulus-return operations actually introduced here.

The new public layer has a distinct admission record for source origins, code, proof files, independent audit verdicts and exact receipts. Rehashing data alone grants no authority. Candidate files are preserved unchanged even when a separate final record admits their completed composition. The final coverage ledger must state which layer has been earned.

## Implementation, admission, and adversarial checks (T8)

The new workspace is separate from every inherited source tree. The native physical engine, image theorem, terminal filter, and prior certification ledgers remain sealed. The radius adapter relocates outputs and uses the reviewed 3447-row filter, repriced at each actual h. It validates exact reduced rational frequencies, the physical preparation, frame, image, source origin, and before/after engine hashes.

The public radius_evaluator_v3.py admits existing receipts only through the distinct source-review manifest. A newly admitted source must be generated by the reviewed implementation. A fresh process may also reuse an already admitted exact sample, which is reported as reuse. Arbitrarily copied or self-rehashed caches do not acquire authority. Scalar certificates are canonically reconstructed from their physical budget; root and modulus certificates are reconstructed from their admitted scalar and exact fiber. No supplied status flag substitutes for that reconstruction. The first public version admitted an optional review dictionary without canonically reloading its authority; version two repairs that bypass by reloading and validating the current reviewed manifest at each admission boundary. The earlier interface and the rejection controls are preserved as separate evidence.

A fresh public continuation with a fixed reference slope remained valid but converged slowly: after four physical steps its root disk had radius about 5.99×10^{−14}, above the requested 10^{−16}. Version two uses an interpolated slope only to propose the next exact tilt. Every accepted root disk still requires its fresh or admitted physical scalar enclosure and the proved factor floor. A faster proposal is not itself a stronger certificate; fresh execution outcomes are reported only from their saved receipts. Four iterations reduced the certified root radius to less than 1.47444 × 10^{−18}, meeting the requested 10^{−16} target. This success belongs to that executed input, not to a uniform iteration-count guarantee.

Fresh-process CLI reproduction then exposed a distinct precision-dependent false refusal in version two: the admitted image-refined scalar was rejected at the caller’s default 53-bit context, and also at 128 or 256 bits, because a recomputed interval upper bound became needlessly wider than its valid saved bound. Version three sets the reviewed admission precision to 768 bits immediately before constructing and executing Admission.scalar. ## Independent checks and limits of independence (M11)

The geometry producer uses exact cardinal polynomials with interval coefficient contractions. The independent geometry reader reconstructs the radius polynomial in a Chebyshev basis and bounds it on trigonometric panels. The h-jet audit reconstructs the discrete Fourier contractions from every admitted physical node and separately reassembles the h = 0 Toeplitz constant. The logarithmic higher-tilt majorants and expanded-ellipse bounds have independent 1024-bit evaluations.

Original-Haar challenges at selected preparations do not merely replay the transformed prefix. They compare independent original-angular and finite Acb source calculations with the native source contract. The endpoint point zero is independently linked through strict containment in its original Haar uniqueness disk. These checks share Arb special functions and inherited analytic identities where stated; they are not independent proofs of the entire foundational HaarCritical programme.

Successful numerical agreement is never the remainder estimate. In particular, the atlas continuum follows from interval-wide inequalities and analytic remainders, not interpolation of root values. The same-source agreement of two terminal calculations does not independently verify their common prefix.

The new public arithmetic interface is near_zero_evaluator_v4.py. Why correlated quotient bounds matter

A deliberately looser aggregation fails even for the successful outer construction. The global minimum linear floor times 0.012 is about 1.69289 10^{−5}, while the sum of the separately maximized centre and nonlinear bounds is about 1.72610 10^{−5}. That premature separation would fail. If the centre and nonlinear bounds are first added on the same arc, their global maximum is instead about 1.42321 10^{−5} and this coarser correlated comparison also passes. The execution retains the sharper arcwise quotients B_{j}/a_{j} for its canonical root envelope. The normalized maximum-modulus argument in Theorem Q4.1 does not assume that maxima at different parameter cells occur together.

## Verification, interface and reproducibility (Q9)

The public correlated_atlas_evaluator.py provides exact-input coverage, zero-tube, physical-root, modulus and scalar-classification operations. It checks the canonical inherited outer authority and the new independent review before returning a certificate. A root refinement is accepted only from a separately admitted physical scalar with matching rank, order, tilt, radius, origin and complete budget.

The interface refuses binary floating inputs, unsupported parameter domains, unadmitted candidate scalars, changed dependencies, missing continuum panels, a diagnostic probe presented as a theorem, wrong-fiber root reuse, and unsupported relative claims. Exact rationals are preserved; the original native signed-frequency restriction remains a source-engine contract and is not bypassed by rounding a requested physical radius.

The independent tests also challenge omitted direction averaging, conjugated tilt, altered physical normalization, relabeled precision and zeroed arithmetic allowances. Failed configurations and early diagnostic probes are retained with their original status. The successful continuum result is not inferred by interpolating a finite collection of roots.

Resource record

On the available execution host, the final producing model and physical return reconstruction took about 24 seconds, followed by about 194 seconds for all 4096 outer parameter cells. The independent full geometry took about 285 seconds, with a separately executed 369-packet physical-return audit. These timings are observations, not complexity or performance guarantees. Six initial fresh physical preparations and readouts completed in about 131 seconds with parallel workers.

The numerical runtime was Python 3.12.14, python-flint 0.9.0 and NumPy 2.3.5; native sources used g++ 14.2.0 with the inherited arithmetic flags. The trusted computational base is Arb/Acb, their underlying libraries, the sealed native arithmetic contracts and the cited analytic proofs. This package is an executed interval verification record, not a formal proof-assistant development.

Exact restart and limits

The compact verification distribution is an overlay. It preserves the five prerequisite archive hashes and all new code, mathematical notes, producing and independent receipts, source origins, failures and review bindings. The restart document gives a clean recovery order, public smoke tests and full continuum reproduction com-mands. Historical absolute workspace paths in old audit records are provenance; portable launchers bind only the recovered filesystem location without changing mathematical inputs or sealed source bytes.

No theorem is claimed beyond |h| ≤ 0.2 or beyond the radius interval [0.899, 0.9]. No sharp new global bound for α_{h} or α_{z} over that full domain is released. The stronger inner modulus factor is not silently substituted into the outer public dispatcher. Very close to the branch, a physical query may still require the inherited high-precision source selector or image refinement; the present two off-zero queries already meet their targets with their executed resources.

The most direct continuation is to make the correlated terminal and parameter-return machinery reusable in a resource-adaptive physical evaluator, with locally admitted order/radius charts and tighter branch derivative information. Broader order or radius continuation then requires new strict inequalities, not extrapolation of this certificate. Practical low-rank completion, broader exact frequency support and remaining high-precision scalar compositions remain separate parts of the original programme and were not diverted into during this investigation.

## Integer order as a physical invariant subspace

Theorem 23.5 (rank-four propagation on the exceptional order). Take the upper and lower polygons from 11/25 to 14/25 through 1/2 ± 3i/50. At h = 2, the angularly prepared solution on each path has a representation by seven two-component linear equations, valid for every complex s. Its polynomial readouts give the entire 35-component physical vector and the original scalar at the exit. ^{G}i^{ = a}i,+^{F}i,+^{G}i−1^{ + a}i,−^{F}i,−^{G}i−1^{.}_{∑}

At nonzero u the physical connection applied successively gives G_{i}(u) = u^{j≤iqj}W_{i}(u). Holomorphy extends this identity to the full disk. In particular the first p Taylor coefficients of G_{k} vanish on the true input. This compatibility is obtained on the connected state at each wall. It need not hold for an arbitrary branch at an interior stage.

For a germ H write H_{j} = [u^{j}]H and 𝒟_{p}H(u) = (H(u) −^{∑}_{j<p}u^{j}H_{j})/u^{p}, with value H_{p} at zero. Transport the data (H , . . . , H , 𝒟 H) throughout. If a path generator is B + uD, the coefficient equations are H^{′} = 0 p−1 p e_{j}

B H + DH, with H = 0, and (𝒟 H)^{′} = (B + uD)𝒟 H + DH. Multiplication by a holomorphic scalar e j j−1 −1 p e p p−1 weight a uses ordinary truncated convolution and

```text
_{∑}p−1
𝒟_{p}(aH) = a(u)𝒟_{p}H(u) + H_{j}𝒟_{p−j}a(u).
j=0
```

All derivatives here are of the source or of known weights and equations. The readout 𝒟_{p}G_{k} is precisely W_{k}. Low-order coefficients may instead be dropped by exact degree shifts after each exceptional wall, reducing the remaining order depth by one. The p = 0 case is ordinary transport.

For a certified error statement choose analytic finite approximants to each input, weight and transfer on |u| ≤A. Let L_{i} bound the norm of the exact ith combined weighted map and d_{i} bound its approximation error there. With incoming norm at most M, analytic input error at most d_{0}, and empty products understood as one, the final numerator error on that disk is bounded by

```text
_{∏} [∏_{∏} ]
E = d_{0} (L_{i} + d_{i}) + M (L_{i} + d_{i}) − L_{i} .
i i i
```

This follows from the ordered-product difference and requires no mutual commutation. Cauchy’s coefficient estimate gives an outgoing error at most E/[A^{p}(1 −r/A)] in the divided data on |u| ≤r. It applies to analytic truncation errors even when the approximate numerator has nonzero low-order coefficients. The finite arithmetic of the derivative algorithm is enclosed separately at the query. This proves an error-transfer law; its constants require evaluation on each proposed multiwall chart. □

As an illustration of possible multiplicity, rank seven has successive positive walls at 1/7, 3/7, 5/7. At e = 1/2 the first and third phase denominators vanish while the middle one is regular. Here two order derivatives suffice for the chain under the stated chart and fibre hypotheses. The statement fixes the missing source information; it supplies no executed rank-seven certificate.
